audiences.label: People using the skill in Claude Code
Maintainers of the Shiplog CI workflow

releases.summary: Slack announcements, faster drafting, archive pages and audience feeds

entries.title: Announce releases in Slack
entries.description: After a release is published, Shiplog can post it to one or more Slack channels. Each channel only gets the changes for its audiences, and action-required changes come first with their deadline. You see a preview of every message and nothing is sent until you confirm. Webhook URLs and tokens stay in environment variables or CI secrets, never in the repository.

entries.title: Import an existing CHANGELOG.md
entries.description: Ask Claude to import your Keep a Changelog file and each version becomes a Shiplog release. Old entries don't say who is affected, so every imported entry is marked for review, and the validator lists them until you confirm the impact.

entries.title: A feed for each audience
entries.description: Besides the main feed, each audience now gets its own Atom feed with only the changes that affect it, plus changes for everyone. The changelog page links to all of them, so admins can subscribe to admin changes only.

entries.title: Translate the changelog page and get link previews
entries.description: Every label on the page, including month names and the date format, can be translated in the config. Pages now include Open Graph and canonical tags, so links shared in chat or social apps show a proper preview.

entries.title: Autocomplete for release files in your editor
entries.description: Release files and the config now point to a JSON Schema, so editors like VS Code suggest field names and flag mistakes while you type.

entries.title: Releases are drafted faster, with fewer questions
entries.description: Claude now reads a compact one-line-per-change summary instead of every commit in full, and asks all its questions about impact in one message. If you already gave the version or impact details, it doesn't ask again. When the GitHub CLI is available, pull request titles, descriptions and labels are fetched in a single request.

entries.title: Changes are grouped by pull request
entries.description: Repositories that use merge commits or squash merges now get one suggested entry per pull request, titled with the pull request's title, instead of one per commit. Previously the pull request titles in merge commits were skipped.

entries.title: Older releases move to yearly archive pages
entries.description: The main changelog page now shows the latest 20 releases. Older releases are on one page per year, linked at the bottom of every page. Feeds and CHANGELOG.md link to the right page. Links to an older release on the main page now land on the main page without jumping to it; set page_size to 0 in the config to keep everything on one page.

entries.title: Python 3.10 or newer
entries.description: Shiplog is now tested on Python 3.10 through 3.13. Python 3.8 and 3.9 are no longer supported.
entries.action: If you run Shiplog or its CI workflow on Python 3.8 or 3.9, switch to Python 3.10 or newer.

entries.title: More helpful validation messages
entries.description: Validation messages now name the file and the entry title, so problems are easy to find. The validator also warns when the newest release has a deadline that has passed, and when a deprecation doesn't say what to use instead.

entries.title: CI workflow template reads full history and can post to Slack
entries.description: New workflows fetch the full git history and tags, and include an optional step that announces tagged releases in Slack. Existing workflows keep working. To get the new template and scripts, run the setup again with the force option.

entries.title: The changelog page no longer changes on every render
entries.description: Pages used to include the date they were built, so rendering unchanged releases on another day produced a diff. The footer now shows the latest release date, and re-rendering gives identical files.

entries.title: Better version suggestions
entries.description: After a pre-release such as 1.2.0-beta.1, the suggested version is now 1.2.0 instead of 1.2.1 or 1.3.0. First releases are suggested as 0.1.0, tags on other branches are ignored, and shallow CI checkouts get a clear message instead of a wrong range.

entries.title: Fewer false warnings about jargon
entries.description: Phrases like "our #1 priority", product names that contain words such as Hotfix, and standards like UTF-8 or ISO-8601 no longer trigger warnings. You can also list accepted terms in the config.
